title: 'MPs sleeping': Delhi transport bodies to march to Parliament on Aug 4 against E20 fuel
content: Delhi transport groups will march to Parliament on August 4.  They demand the withdrawal of ethanol-blended petrol from the market.  Concerns about vehicle problems and mileage reduction are being raised.  The government defends the E20 fuel program as safe and beneficial.  This protest aims to highlight issues with the mandated fuel blend.

title: CWG: Gyaneshwari wins silver as India claims 4th weightlifting medal
content: It was India's fourth weightlifting medal at the ongoing Commonwealth Games in Glasgow. Earlier, Mirabai Chanu (women's 48kg - gold), Rishikanta Singh (men's 60kg - silver) and Muthupandi Raja (men's 65kg - silver) had also finished on the podium in their respective categories.

title: Unhappy with $7bn collateral data centre bill in ‘America's Dairyland’, Oracle goes to court
content: Oracle challenges Wisconsin regulators over a massive collateral requirement for its new AI data center. The company faces significant annual costs due to strict credit rules for utility We Energies. Regulators aim to prevent local customers from subsidizing large tech infrastructure projects. This dispute highlights growing concerns over tech companies' financial commitments and infrastructure costs. Many states are now implementing similar regulations for major technology firms.

title: Watch: CJP party videos post-Pradhan's resignation surface; Saurav Das seen dancing
content: A video shows CJP leaders dancing after their protest ended, sparking social media debate. Critics questioned the celebrations' appropriateness given the movement's focus on student issues. Supporters defended the gathering as a deserved moment of relief after a difficult campaign. Political figures raised concerns about the protest's funding and the timing of the festivities. CJP leaders responded by stating younger generations protest and organize differently.

title: Pregnant woman among three stabbed in Paris knife attack; suspect detained
content: A man was arrested after stabbing three women near Paris's Porte de Clichy on Monday. One victim, believed to be pregnant, is in critical condition after the attack. The 31-year-old suspect, who reportedly has mental health issues, was apprehended at the scene. Police found two knives in the possession of the arrested individual. An investigation into the incident has been officially opened by authorities.

title: 'Could open floodgates': Why HC quashed Vijay govt jobs for kin of Karur stampede victims
content: The Madras High Court's Madurai Bench recently invalidated the allocation of government jobs to the relatives of victims from the Karur stampede. The ruling highlighted concerns over constitutional principles of equality and the right to equal opportunity in public service. The court pointed out that current waiting lists for compassionate appointments had been ignored.

title: Jeff Bezos ex-wife MacKenzie Scott helped write a 'donation playbook' for Snap founder
content: Snap co-founder Evan Spiegel and Miranda Kerr have donated $550 million to erase medical debt. This significant contribution will benefit over 261,000 Californians facing financial hardship.  The donation follows a model pioneered by MacKenzie Scott, who has given billions to nonprofits.  The funds will be channeled through Undue Medical Debt, a prominent organization.  This initiative targets vulnerable residents, alleviating burdens of unpayable medical bills.

title: Inside Jeff Bezos’ 10,000-year clock being built in a Texas mountain
content: Jeff Bezos is championing an extraordinary endeavor by funding a 10,000-year clock hidden inside a Texas mountain. This visionary project seeks to inspire humanity towards long-term thinking and sustainability. Harnessing natural energy, the clock will tick continuously for thousands of years, featuring a unique bell mechanism that creates countless melodies. Its design emphasizes durability, serving as a poignant commentary on the fleeting nature of modern existence.

title: Imported for fur, giant rodent now devastates US wetlands
content: Nutria, large rodents introduced for fur farming, now infest forty US states and Canada.  These prolific breeders destroy vital wetland vegetation and agricultural crops like rice.  Their burrowing weakens levees and dams, posing risks to infrastructure and public safety.  Eradication efforts involve trapping, detection dogs, and bounty programs to control populations.  These invasive creatures have caused millions of dollars in damage across affected regions.

title: Canada clarifies work permit rules for international students after rejections
content: Canada's immigration authority has clarified international student work rules.  Unauthorized work can lead to serious consequences and future permit refusals.  Portage College advised protesting Indian students to seek legal counsel.  Students must retain all important documents for future applications.  The college is seeking further clarification on this ongoing issue.

title: Meet the Kolkata teacher who transformed children’s lives in the Sundarbans with a dream
content: A Kolkata teacher started a mission to educate children in the Sundarbans. She established a school which grew to serve hundreds of island children. The organization faced challenges including a cyclone and a pandemic. It expanded its reach by setting up new centers on the islands. This initiative provides quality education to many first-generation learners.

title: 'Busy planting seeds of hate': FIFA backs Trump-Balogun decision, hits back at critics
content: In a 900-word statement published across a 15-page post on his Instagram account and on FIFA’s website late Sunday, Infantino said FIFA had succeeded in staging the World Cup and bringing people together.

title: From pacifist to talks of going nuclear: China shaken as Japan breaks 80-yr-old shackles
content: Japan is shifting away from its long-standing pacifist security doctrine, with increasing defense budgets and a major enhancement of military skills. The nation has restarted arms exports and is forming a dedicated intelligence agency. China perceives these changes as a profound provocation and an emerging strategy, sparked by modern threats and regional shifts in the geopolitical landscape.

title: Ram Charan undergoes wrist surgery, begins rehabilitation before returning to work
content: Ram Charan successfully underwent wrist surgery in Coimbatore on Sunday.  His injury worsened during the shooting of his latest release, Peddi.  Expert doctors, including a specialist from Miami, performed the complex procedure.  He is now recovering well and advised complete rest for several weeks.  Ram Charan will resume shooting after receiving medical clearance from doctors.

title: 'Want him to improve his fitness': Laxman identifies key area for Sooryavanshi
content: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi impressed with his batting performances against Zimbabwe.  Stand-in coach VVS Laxman highlighted fitness as an area for improvement.  The young player showed great commitment and desire to contribute to the team.  Sooryavanshi also excelled in the Under-19 World Cup and IPL.  Improving fitness will be vital for his career's continued growth.

title: 'Ewwww, who is birthing & raising them?' Kangana calls Gen Z protest reels 'puke inducing'
content: Actor-politician Kangana Ranaut criticized Gen Z protests and the Cockroach Janta Party. She described their protest reels as "puke inducing" and "crass" on Instagram. Ranaut also mocked the protesters' use of the "cockroach" metaphor. The CJP recently called off its agitation after discussions with Union ministers. Their principal demand was met with the education minister's resignation.

title: How geopolitics and RBI are shaping Rupee ahead of MPC
content: Analysts anticipate the Indian rupee entering a stable phase soon.  Global crude oil prices will continue to significantly influence the currency's movement.  Sustained high oil prices may increase inflation and widen India's current account deficit.  However, a steep depreciation in the rupee is not expected by experts.  The Reserve Bank of India's monetary policy meeting in August is also a key event.

title: Jantar Mantar volunteer alleges police picked him up, left him in Mussoorie
content: A man distributing food at Jantar Mantar claims police picked him up Friday night. He alleged being blindfolded and taken to Mussoorie, where he was questioned. An officer reportedly asked about his funding sources and food distribution methods. Junaid stated he returned to Delhi on Saturday after being left in Mussoorie. Police are currently investigating the allegations made by the food distributor.

title: Dubai-Mumbai IndiGo flight makes emergency landing after smoke in cargo hold
content: An IndiGo flight traveling from Dubai to Mumbai made an unexpected landing in Rajkot due to smoke detected in the cargo hold. Thankfully, all 194 individuals onboard—passengers and crew alike—exited safely, with no injuries reported. Emergency responders swiftly arrived at Rajkot Airport to assist those affected. Currently, the passengers are in the terminal, waiting for the next steps regarding their onward journey.

title: Missiles from cargo planes: The new strike idea that could interest India
content: Modern warfare increasingly relies on smart, autonomous weapons designed to disable an adversary’s ability to retaliate. India’s Operation Sindoor in May 2025 reflected this logic, beginning with strikes on terror infrastructure and expanding to Pakistani military assets such as radar sites, airbases and command centres. Even temporary damage to runways or radars can create operational gaps, enabling follow-on strikes. Launch platforms are critical: India fields BrahMos missiles from land, sea and modified Su-30MKIs, while Rafales carry SCALP missiles. To expand salvo capacity, the US developed Rapid Dragon, a palletised missile system for cargo aircraft, now evolving into Dragon Cart. Brazil’s C-390 project with Anduril explores similar concepts. Such systems could complement fighters by turning transports into “missile trucks,” boosting strike volume.

title: NEET leak row puts NDA families in spotlight as daughters back protest
content: Daughters of two politicians publicly broke ranks over the NEET protest demonstrations. Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma defended his cabinet colleague Keshab Mahanta's position. Odisha BJP MP Aparajita Sarangi's office backed her daughter's right to express views. The daughters voiced support for student protesters and criticized the central government's actions. Party officials stated these views were personal and did not reflect internal discontent.

title: India's housing squeeze: Why more young Indians are choosing to live with their parents
content: Housing costs in India now exceed average earnings, making independent living a significant challenge.  Young Indians face difficulties building wealth and saving for their futures.  This situation compels many to remain with their parents for extended periods.  Simultaneously, younger adults often support ageing relatives, adding financial strain.  Innovative housing solutions and intergenerational collaboration are needed to address these pressures.

title: Delhi man poses as SP, invokes DGP’s name to restore electricity to wife’s shop
content: A Delhi man was arrested for masquerading as a Himachal Police officer after he contacted a Gurgaon SHO to restore power to his wife's shop. Presenting himself as SP Chandan Singh, he attempted to exert undue influence. However, the police caught onto his ruse, leading to a case being registered. He later confessed to the impersonation when the power situation was confirmed.

title: Ram Temple donation 'theft' case: SC tells SIT to submit status report within 2 weeks
content: The Supreme Court has directed the Special Investigation Team to submit a status report. This report concerns the alleged theft of offerings at the Ayodhya Ram Temple. The court issued this direction while hearing petitions seeking a court-monitored investigation. The Uttar Pradesh government will add a forensic auditor to the SIT. This SIT currently comprises three IPS officers.

title: Patrick Mahomes, Brittany donate $1.625M to create opportunities for children
content: Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes made a lasting impact off the football field with a $1.625 million partnership through the 15 and the Mahomies Foundation. Announced in October 2023, the initiative supports Boys & Girls Clubs in East Texas, Greater Kansas City and Lubbock, while also funding scholarships for hundreds of children and upgrading Club facilities. Here's how the Kansas City Chiefs star and his wife turned their hometown ties into a long-term commitment to help young people build brighter futures.

title: ITR filing deadline: What happens if you don’t file your income tax return by July 31?
content: ITR filing FY 2025-26: Many individuals are unsure about whether they are required to file their income tax return or not at a particular income level. An income tax return needs to be filed if your taxable income is more than the basic exemption limit.

title: 'Thank you VVS sir': Iyer credits Laxman after India's 3-0 Zimbabwe sweep
content: India secured a commanding 3-0 T20I series victory against Zimbabwe. Captain Shreyas Iyer and interim coach VVS Laxman exchanged praise for their leadership. An inexperienced Indian squad achieved the clean sweep with a final T20I win. Laxman commended Iyer's optimistic attitude and leadership throughout the series. Iyer thanked Laxman for his motivating influence and inspiration to the team.

title: India gets a lower US tariff; here's why textile exporters are still worried
content: India's textile sector faces US market pressure despite a 10% tariff rate.  Competitors received tariff-rate quota exemptions which India missed out on.  This absence weakens India's overall competitiveness against rival nations.  However, India remains a relative beneficiary of the revised US tariff framework.  Future investigations could expose India to additional tariffs, necessitating trade deal negotiations.

title: Jana Nayagan Day 5: Thalapathy Vijay's final film nears Rs 150 cr India gross

Its India net collection reached one hundred twenty-six crore rupees by Monday.  The Tamil version contributed significantly to the film's overall earnings.  This political action drama is Vijay's last film before entering politics.

title: How many more lives? Why Delhi's open drains and deadly pits keep claiming young victims
content: Young lives are lost due to Delhi's recurring civic failures and negligence. Open drains and unsafe construction sites pose deadly hazards for commuters. Preventable tragedies highlight a lack of essential safety measures and enforcement. Multiple agencies and contractors share responsibility for these ongoing failures. Consistent implementation of safety standards is urgently needed to prevent further deaths.

title: 'Rajghat, then back to mountains': Sonam Wangchuk discharged from Medanta Hospital
content: Sonam Wangchuk has been discharged from Medanta Hospital after his hunger strike. He will now visit Rajghat to honour Mahatma Gandhi before returning home. Wangchuk led a 26-day hunger strike demanding the education minister's resignation. The protest concluded after successful talks between the CJP and the Centre. Dharmendra Pradhan later resigned, and Pralhad Joshi was appointed as the new minister.

His performance showcased adaptability to different match conditions and bowling plans.
